title: Obliviousness of the masked clock
statement: Let $A$ be an alphabet, $W$ a finite Turing machine over $A$, and $z\in A$. The machine obtained from $W$ by replacing every nonblank symbol read on the input tape by $z$ before applying $W$’s transition function is oblivious: for any two inputs of equal length and every time $t\in\mathbb N$, its input-head positions and all its work-tape head positions agree. No halting assumption is required.
hypotheses_covered: W is a finite Turing machine over A
z is a symbol in A
replaced:
For every machine $W$ over an alphabet $A$ and every symbol $z \in A$, the masked
clock of $W$ with mask $z$ is oblivious: on any two inputs of the same length its
input-head position and all of its work-head positions agree at every time. No
halting hypothesis is required.
